bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on public procurement cycles and government project approvals — Large public-infrastructure projects involve extended tendering, technical and commercial evaluation, administrative approvals and contractual finalisation, so the timing of opportunities is difficult to predict. Management notes several opportunities were delayed by code-of-conduct constraints over the past twelve months, and water-sector implementation remains dependent on public funding, project approvals and local utility capability.
- Client contract termination and concentration in institutional customers — Listed in Risks & Concerns as termination of contracts without cause, with little or no notice, or with heavy penalties. The business is weighted towards government, PSU and infrastructure enterprise clients with 100+ active projects, so contract-level actions carry disproportionate revenue impact.
- Increasing competitive intensity across the infrastructure-technology value chain — Engineering companies, IT service providers, specialist GIS firms, software OEMs, consulting organisations and new AI-led companies are increasingly competing across overlapping areas, pressuring win rates and pricing.
- Rapid technology obsolescence and the cost of staying current — Artificial intelligence, cloud architectures, sensors, engineering platforms and software environments evolve quickly, requiring continuous evaluation of emerging technologies and recurring investment in new tools, platforms and specialist skills.
- Availability of specialised multidisciplinary talent — The convergence of engineering, GIS, cloud, AI, automation and domain knowledge increases demand for multidisciplinary professionals whose skills may take considerable time to develop, constraining the ability to scale delivery.
- Cybersecurity and data sovereignty exposure — Infrastructure systems increasingly contain sensitive operational and spatial data, and greater connectivity creates additional requirements around cybersecurity, access management, traceability and data residency. The Company reports no cyber security incidents, breaches or loss of data during FY 2025-26.
- Foreign exchange volatility and international expansion exposure — Flagged in Risks & Concerns as fluctuations in currency exchange rates affecting costs and revenues; the Company has operations across India, USA, UK, Germany and UAE with subsidiaries reporting in SGD, USD, Euro and GBP, and is expanding into MEA and ASEAN.
- Automotive market cyclicality affecting the Mobility Engineering business — Automotive engineering remains influenced by underlying vehicle demand and customer product-development cycles; changes in EV adoption, technology investment or product strategies may influence engineering expenditure, and the sector is exposed to commodity-price movements and differing EV-adoption rates across regions.
- Regulatory, licensing and contingent-liability exposure — Risks & Concerns lists alterations in domestic and foreign policies, laws, regulations and tax regimes; failure to secure or renew essential approvals and licenses; and realization of unanticipated legal or contractual obligations. The Company is not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee under SEBI LODR.
- Data quality and legacy-system dependence in delivery — Digital twins, analytics and GeoAI rely on reliable source information; incomplete asset records, inconsistent data standards and fragmented legacy systems at client utilities can increase implementation effort and reduce output quality, and the effectiveness of digital twins depends on completeness and interoperability of underlying asset data.

business.body:
- "Unlike any other player, we operate at the intersection of" core engineering, geospatial intelligence, artificial intelligence and infrastructure and mobility systems - delivering "a full-stack geospatial AI platform powering intelligent infrastructure".
- Framed as "Consistent Results in an Inconsistent Market": while most players struggle with slow procurement cycles, funding winter and delayed decision-making, the company claims a healthy pipeline across Government, PSU and Infra Enterprises and early international traction in MEA despite macro headwinds.
- "CS TECH Ai has delivered continuous 3 years of positive revenue growth" and has "100+ projects being executed with zero client churn" - summarised as "Repeatable, Predictable, Proven."
- Problem framing: infrastructure planning is "outdated, slow, and fragmented", GIS systems are "passive and underutilized", data sources (satellites, drones, IoT) are under-leveraged and manual decision-making drives cost, inefficiency and risk; the company's answer is AI plus geospatial intelligence "to drive smarter and faster decisions at scale".
- Delivery model is stated as "We don't just build tech - we engineer outcomes", built on real-time data integration from drones/satellites/sensors, AI-driven digital twins of assets, cities and utilities, visual dashboards for smart decisioning, and actionable insights for planning, maintenance and operations.

business.body: Ceinsys Tech Limited operates at the forefront of technology-driven solutions, specializing in geospatial services, industrial automation and infrastructure development. Its geo-mobility value chain spans end-to-end GIS data services, enterprise Web GIS and decision support systems, full-vehicle product engineering and industrial automation, delivered to governments, smart cities, utilities, mobility customers and industrial asset owners. It has been at the centre of India's flagship national water infrastructure programmes including the Jal Jeevan Mission and AMRUT 2.0, backed by integrated decision support systems.

business.body:
- **Enterprise Geospatial:** Remote Sensing and Photogrammetry, LiDAR Data Engineering, 3D Modelling & Digital Twin, AI/ML Change Detection, Enterprise Solutions (Spatial Analytics & Dashboards, Mobile Apps and Geoportal, WebGIS, Intelligent Decision Support System, DPMS & CDE), ICCC
- **Water:** Consultancy for Water & Waste Water (Engineering Survey, DPR, Project Management Consultancy), Consultancy for Water Resources (Flood and Yield studies, DPR, PMC), Consultancy for Water Quality (GIS-based field survey, water quality testing, DPR), NRW / Reforms (NRW assessment and reduction strategy, leak detection), Smart Water (Field instrumentation, IoT & SCADA, smart consumer meters, leak detection), Software Solutions (Water billing software, design software, Web-GIS application development)
- **Transportation:** Digital Project Management System (BIM-based 4D/5D design management, CDE, GIS-based construction monitoring), Road Asset Management System (DAQ using LiDAR, NSV, FWD, MBIU; PCI indexation; PMU set-up), ITS: ITMS/ATMS/MLFF (traffic monitoring and management, enforcement, incident and emergency management), Consultancy (planning and feasibility studies, engineering design, project management and operations support)
- **Web GIS Integrated Solutions:** Decision support systems, Enterprise administrative portals, Utilities, Municipal, ULB and agriculture domain solutions
- **Engineering Solutions:** Non-Revenue Water consulting, Urban and rural water supply and sewage scheme DPRs, SCADA and automation for water and electric transmission and distribution, Smart water solutions and Advanced Metering Infrastructure, Roads and Highways DPRs, Road Asset Management System (RAMS), Corridor mapping, 5D BIM and CDE for Transport, Infrastructure and Construction, Project Management Consultancy (PMC) and Third-Party Inspection (TPI)
- **New-age Technology Solutions:** LiDAR data capturing and processing, UAV data capturing and processing, Laser scanning and 3D modelling, Point cloud extraction, Photogrammetry solutions, Digital Twin Engineering, AI/ML-based solutions
- **Mobility / Automotive Engineering Services:** Product engineering (concept generation, detail design, feasibility studies, packaging, integration), Virtual verification through CAE/FEA/CFD and change management, Manufacturing engineering (consulting, plant design and optimization, tooling design, robotics automation, simulation), IoT and IIoT for Industry 4.0, AI-based computer vision solutions

outlook.body:

outlook.body: CS TECH Ai's expansion is capability- and footprint-led rather than plant-led. Growth has been strategically inorganic: AllyGrow Technologies was acquired in FY2021-22 adding vehicle product engineering and industrial automation, the assets of VTS, a US-based reality capture firm, were acquired in FY2023-24 bringing 3D scanning and digital twin expertise, and in FY2025-26 the Company mobilised INR 2,380 million for further acquisition, capability enhancement and international expansion, with additional acquisitions planned across geospatial, mobility and technology domains. In July 2026 the Board approved the formation of a joint venture with AI Fabrik, Inc., USA to establish an AI Neo Cloud sovereign AI infrastructure and services platform in India for government, citizen services, enterprise and cybersecurity and defence applications, approving an initial investment of `25 crore to be made in a phased manner. The Company established a dedicated vertical for artificial intelligence, machine learning and embedded electronics, and is developing two emerging sub-domains, Satellite and Data as a Service and Mining Intelligence. Internationally it is forming strategic alliances in MEA and ASEAN, engaging GIS consulting firms as channel partners, and establishing a presence in Saudi Arabia and Dubai, alongside a partnership with Tech Mahindra announced in January 2026 and a strategic MoU with Singapore-based Aetosky; it operates offices in India, the US, the UAE and Germany. In India it is expanding its government empanelment base to access a wider range of schemes. On 19 February 2026 the Company's equity shares were listed on the National Stock Exchange, giving it dual BSE and NSE listing, and after the year end, on April 18 2026, it made a further investment of USD 2.161 million in its wholly owned foreign subsidiary Technology Associates Inc., USA. Consolidated capital expenditure on assets during FY2025-26 was ` 1,356 Lakhs, compared with ` 2,184 Lakhs in FY2024-25, and the Company reports no capital commitments as at the end of any of the reported years.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Infrastructure programmes are increasingly expected to incorporate digital planning, monitoring and asset information alongside conventional engineering, supported by effective public capital expenditure of approximately `17.15 lakh crore and wider use of PM GatiShakti
- Geospatial technology is expected to become more deeply embedded in infrastructure, utilities and enterprise operations, with Earth Observation, reality capture, GIS, BIM, AI and digital twins expanding spatial intelligence from mapping towards automated interpretation and lifecycle decision-making
- GeoAI is expected to become particularly important as the volume and frequency of spatial data continue to increase
- In Water, expanding network coverage is shifting the focus from asset creation towards service reliability, NRW reduction, pressure and flow monitoring, water-quality assurance, wastewater reuse and long-term operations
- In Energy, renewable integration, transmission expansion and storage are increasing network complexity, supporting continued adoption of digital asset management, SCADA, IoT, geospatial analysis and predictive analytics
- Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028 for 100% rural water coverage ensures sustained demand for the Company's water infrastructure capabilities
- The National Geospatial Mission's focus on core geospatial infrastructure and datasets directly matches the Company's core competency
- Government modernisation of land records, urban planning and infrastructure design adds further project pipelines
- India's 340 GW renewable energy target by 2030 is boosting demand in water and clean energy, both areas of established delivery capability
- Electrification, software-defined architectures and manufacturing automation are reshaping automotive engineering requirements, making the Mobility Engineering opportunity driven by rising engineering complexity rather than vehicle volumes alone
- Data-centre and AI infrastructure investment is creating additional demand for power, cooling, engineering and digital asset-management systems
- Several opportunities delayed by code-of-conduct constraints over the past twelve months are now showing positive traction
- Mobility and Product Services operate predominantly through recurring customer commitments rather than large project-based orders, providing a run-rate revenue base outside the conventional project order book
- Working capital remains an area of continued focus as project billing is linked to achievement and certification of contractual milestones; the FY26 scale-up increased trade receivables and unbilled revenue with billing conversion expected as milestones complete
- The FY2026-27 industry outlook remains constructive but uncertain — geopolitical conditions, procurement timelines, technology cycles, financing costs and customer investment decisions will continue to influence the timing of opportunities
- Closing order book of INR 8,760 million provides strong revenue visibility into the year ahead
- CS TECH Ai entered FY27 with a closing disclosed order book of `876 crore, excluding annual and other customer commitments in Mobility and Product Services
- The Company enters FY2026-27 with a strong order book, an improving cash position and a pipeline expected to convert meaningfully in FY27, with several funnel opportunities proposed to result in award of contracts

deepdive.thesis: Ceinsys Tech Limited is a geospatial technology company that provides innovative solutions for infrastructure development, with a strong focus on artificial intelligence and digital transformation. The company has delivered consistent revenue growth and has a healthy pipeline of projects across government, PSU, and infra enterprises. With its full-stack geospatial AI platform, Ceinsys Tech Limited is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for intelligent infrastructure solutions.

open.item: The Board approved formation of a joint venture with AI Fabrik, Inc., USA to establish an AI Neo Cloud sovereign AI infrastructure and services platform in India, with an initial investment of `25 crore to be made in a phased manner.

The focus for FY27 will be to convert several opportunities presently in the funnel into award of contracts to build a stronger order book, with the pipeline expected to convert meaningfully during the year.

The Company's priorities for FY27 are conversion of the business funnel into executable contracts, disciplined project delivery, expansion of international operations and development of higher-value digital and IP-led solutions.
The Company entered FY27 with a closing disclosed order book of `876 crore, excluding annual and other customer commitments in Mobility and Product Services, to be converted into revenue.

The Company has initiated a dedicated vertical focused on artificial intelligence, machine learning and embedded electronics, initially developing applications for use across its established infrastructure, geospatial and engineering businesses.

The Board approved an initial investment of `25 crore in the proposed AI Fabrik, Inc. joint venture to establish an AI Neo Cloud sovereign AI infrastructure and services platform in India, to be made in a phased manner.

Management flagged that project billing remains linked to achievement and certification of contractual milestones, with the FY26 scale-up increasing trade receivables and unbilled revenue pending billing conversion.
The AI Fabrik JV company will present its business and investment plan outlining the additional investments required to support the JV's next phase of growth.
In India the Company is expanding its empanelment base to access a wider range of government schemes while building focused partnerships in infrastructure and mobility.
Two emerging sub-domains — Satellite and Data as a Service, and Mining Intelligence — are being developed as long-term growth opportunities supported by Indian policy tailwinds.
Internationally, the Company is forming strategic alliances in MEA and ASEAN, engaging GIS consulting firms as channel partners, and establishing a presence in Saudi Arabia and Dubai.

Additional acquisitions are planned across geospatial, mobility and technology domains, funded from the INR 2,380 million mobilised in FY2025-26 for further acquisition, capability enhancement and international expansion.
Partnership with Tech Mahindra announced in January 2026 to jointly pursue geospatial, AI-driven and digital-twin solutions for infrastructure and enterprise customers across international markets.

At March 31, 2026, `235.05 crore of proceeds from the preferential issuance remained available in bank deposits and current accounts, earmarked as financial flexibility for future strategic initiatives.
In July 2026 the Company received a `67.04 crore Letter of Intent from the Directorate of Urban Administration & Development, Madhya Pradesh for work under PMAY(U).
In May 2026 the Company's US subsidiary received an approximately `4.07 crore order for beta development of a Hybrid Power Transfer Case.
In April 2026 a consortium including CS TECH Ai received an approximately `20.85 crore contract for the Georgia Land Information System, to be executed as an international geospatial engagement.
Strategic MoU entered with Singapore-based Aetosky to jointly pursue Enterprise Geospatial and AI-led opportunities across international markets.
The Company is establishing a presence in Saudi Arabia and Dubai and forming strategic alliances in MEA and ASEAN, engaging GIS consulting firms as channel partners.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Infrastructure programmes are increasingly expected to incorporate digital planning, monitoring and asset information alongside conventional engineering, supported by effective public capital expenditure of approximately `17.15 lakh crore and wider use of PM GatiShakti
- Geospatial technology is expected to become more deeply embedded in infrastructure, utilities and enterprise operations, with Earth Observation, reality capture, GIS, BIM, AI and digital twins expanding spatial intelligence from mapping towards automated interpretation and lifecycle decision-making
- GeoAI is expected to become particularly important as the volume and frequency of spatial data continue to increase
- In Water, expanding network coverage is shifting the focus from asset creation towards service reliability, NRW reduction, pressure and flow monitoring, water-quality assurance, wastewater reuse and long-term operations
- In Energy, renewable integration, transmission expansion and storage are increasing network complexity, supporting continued adoption of digital asset management, SCADA, IoT, geospatial analysis and predictive analytics
- Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028 for 100% rural water coverage ensures sustained demand for the Company's water infrastructure capabilities
- The National Geospatial Mission's focus on core geospatial infrastructure and datasets directly matches the Company's core competency
- Government modernisation of land records, urban planning and infrastructure design adds further project pipelines
- India's 340 GW renewable energy target by 2030 is boosting demand in water and clean energy, both areas of established delivery capability
- Electrification, software-defined architectures and manufacturing automation are reshaping automotive engineering requirements, making the Mobility Engineering opportunity driven by rising engineering complexity rather than vehicle volumes alone
- Data-centre and AI infrastructure investment is creating additional demand for power, cooling, engineering and digital asset-management systems
- Several opportunities delayed by code-of-conduct constraints over the past twelve months are now showing positive traction
- Mobility and Product Services operate predominantly through recurring customer commitments rather than large project-based orders, providing a run-rate revenue base outside the conventional project order book
- Working capital remains an area of continued focus as project billing is linked to achievement and certification of contractual milestones; the FY26 scale-up increased trade receivables and unbilled revenue with billing conversion expected as milestones complete
- The FY2026-27 industry outlook remains constructive but uncertain — geopolitical conditions, procurement timelines, technology cycles, financing costs and customer investment decisions will continue to influence the timing of opportunities
- Closing order book of INR 8,760 million provides strong revenue visibility into the year ahead
- CS TECH Ai entered FY27 with a closing disclosed order book of `876 crore, excluding annual and other customer commitments in Mobility and Product Services
- The Company enters FY2026-27 with a strong order book, an improving cash position and a pipeline expected to convert meaningfully in FY27, with several funnel opportunities proposed to result in award of contracts
- A healthy pipeline across government, PSU and infrastructure enterprise clients, with early international traction in the MEA region
- Order book to be executed as of 31st March 2026 stated at ` 8,760 Mn
- 100+ active project executions maintained with zero client churn
- Major domestic wins during FY26 include an INR 41 crore MHADA contract for an integrated project management and GIS-based digital platform, a multi-year ISRO subscription renewal, extended SWSM Uttar Pradesh rural water-supply inspection and monitoring work estimated at `107.07 crore across three clusters, and a `12.21 crore STP DPR and PMC engagement in Vasai-Virar
- International wins include an INR 21 crore order for the Georgia Land Information System and an INR 4 crore purchase order at the US subsidiary for a hybrid power transfer case
- Private-sector CDE and enterprise-software engagements secured with the Adani Group spanning energy, cement and wider infrastructure requirements

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: CS TECH Ai's expansion is capability- and footprint-led rather than plant-led. Growth has been strategically inorganic: AllyGrow Technologies was acquired in FY2021-22 adding vehicle product engineering and industrial automation, the assets of VTS, a US-based reality capture firm, were acquired in FY2023-24 bringing 3D scanning and digital twin expertise, and in FY2025-26 the Company mobilised INR 2,380 million for further acquisition, capability enhancement and international expansion, with additional acquisitions planned across geospatial, mobility and technology domains. In July 2026 the Board approved the formation of a joint venture with AI Fabrik, Inc., USA to establish an AI Neo Cloud sovereign AI infrastructure and services platform in India for government, citizen services, enterprise and cybersecurity and defence applications, approving an initial investment of `25 crore to be made in a phased manner. The Company established a dedicated vertical for artificial intelligence, machine learning and embedded electronics, and is developing two emerging sub-domains, Satellite and Data as a Service and Mining Intelligence. Internationally it is forming strategic alliances in MEA and ASEAN, engaging GIS consulting firms as channel partners, and establishing a presence in Saudi Arabia and Dubai, alongside a partnership with Tech Mahindra announced in January 2026 and a strategic MoU with Singapore-based Aetosky; it operates offices in India, the US, the UAE and Germany. In India it is expanding its government empanelment base to access a wider range of schemes. On 19 February 2026 the Company's equity shares were listed on the National Stock Exchange, giving it dual BSE and NSE listing, and after the year end, on April 18 2026, it made a further investment of USD 2.161 million in its wholly owned foreign subsidiary Technology Associates Inc., USA. Consolidated capital expenditure on assets during FY2025-26 was ` 1,356 Lakhs, compared with ` 2,184 Lakhs in FY2024-25, and the Company reports no capital commitments as at the end of any of the reported years.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
